_doc: The four representations of `<module>/build/compose-previews/daemon-launch.json`, and the
divergences between them that are correct on purpose. Checked by
`scripts/check-daemon-launch-schema.py`. A debt register, not a config file: an entry is a
claim someone made deliberately, with the reason written down, not an exemption to add when
the check goes red.
schemaVersionSites: every place the descriptor's schema version is declared. The check fails
if any disagrees with the writer, and fails again if a `*DESCRIPTOR_SCHEMA_VERSION` appears
anywhere that is not listed — a new mirror has to be declared here, which is the moment
someone can ask whether it should exist at all. The right long-term number of entries is 2
(the writer, and the TypeScript reader that cannot import Kotlin); the other two are Kotlin
and could read the writer's constant directly if `:render-session-subprocess` and `:cli`
took a dependency on `:gradle-plugin:daemon-launch-builder`. Until then they are mirrors,
and mirrors need a gate rather than a comment asking a human to remember.
readerOnlyFields: a field a reader declares that the plugin's writer never emits. Each must
carry a Kotlin default (or be `?:` in TypeScript), because a plugin-written descriptor will
not contain it. The check enforces that.
writerOnlyFields: a field the writer emits that a reader does not declare. Safe only while
that reader tolerates unknown keys, which the check verifies separately against the JVM
reader's `Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }`.
mirroredConstants: string constants carried inside the descriptor that another module
re-declares privately. Same hazard as the schema version, one level down.

schemaVersionSites.why: The source of truth. `DaemonLaunchBuilder` stamps it into every descriptor it writes, and it participates in `DaemonBootstrapTask`'s up-to-date fingerprint.

The only reader that gates on the version: `daemonProcess.ts` refuses a descriptor whose `schemaVersion` differs. Cannot import the Kotlin constant, so this copy is unavoidable — which is exactly why it needs checking.

`:render-session-subprocess` writes its own descriptors for the bundle daemons it spawns, stamping this private copy. It is one of the twelve published contract modules an extracted preview server links against (#3824), so post-split a stale mirror here is cross-repo version skew no compiler sees.
`compose-preview doctor` reports a descriptor written by a mismatched plugin version. Its comment already says `Keep in sync — bump together`; this makes that enforceable.

jailCommand.writtenBy: the CLI's serve path (ServeBundleDaemon.kt, ServeCommand.kt) via DaemonLaunchDescriptor.jailed()
jailCommand.why: The playground sandbox launches the daemon JVM behind an argv prefix. The Gradle plugin has no sandbox and never writes this; :daemon-client reads it when spawning. Defaults to an empty list, so a plugin-written descriptor parses unchanged.

hardTtlSeconds.writtenBy: the CLI's serve path (ServeBundleDaemon.kt, ServeCommand.kt) via DaemonLaunchDescriptor.jailed()
hardTtlSeconds.why: Wall-clock deadline after which the spawner force-kills a sandboxed daemon. Same sandbox-only origin as jailCommand; null by default.

btaCompile.why: The daemon JVM does read this config, but through flattened `composeai.daemon.bta*` system properties (DefaultBtaCompileService.fromSysprops()), not through the descriptor's nested block — so DaemonLaunchDescriptor has no reason to declare it. The VS Code extension reads the block directly to decide whether calling `compileSources` is worth a round-trip. Survivable only because the JVM reader ignores unknown keys.

SANDBOX_COUNT_PROP.why: The descriptor merges this sysprop in via `withSandboxCount()` and the daemon reads it at boot; its own KDoc says 'both sides MUST agree'. Disagreement silently gives every daemon a pool of one.
